hints.title: Reverse Key Grouping
hints.text: The first group may be shorter than k, but all subsequent groups must contain exactly k characters. Processing backwards automatically aligns the shorter group at the start.

hints.title: Dash Insertion Invariant
hints.text: Traversing alphanumeric characters from right to left, inserting a dash whenever the group counter reaches k preserves equal group lengths.

hints.title: Backward String Assembly Procedure
hints.text: Filter out dashes and convert letters to uppercase. Traverse the cleaned characters from right to left, tracking count of characters in current group. When count equals k, append a dash before adding the next character. Reverse the collected characters and return as a string.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Working forward requires computing remainder modulo k and handling the special first group with conditional branches.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Backward traversal processes each character once in O(N) time with O(N) memory for the output characters.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explain why right-to-left traversal simplifies the short first group and uppercase letters correctly.
